_comment: UNIRA V6.2 scenario definitions. Every parameter not read from data/raw is tagged with an evidence class.

nonmarket_output_sectors.reason: Non-market output volumes are largely measured from inputs (ESA 2010), so measured hourly productivity growth is close to zero by construction and is not evidence about feasible efficiency gains.

imputed_output_sectors.reason: L includes imputed rents of owner-occupiers (no labour input); T output is mostly paid domestic staff valued at wage cost. VA per hour is not a productivity measure here.

weekly_cap_hours.note: UNIRA standard (Constitution Article 6): 6h x 5 days. Since T-10 (2026-11-08) this is the destination, not the starting week; the starting week is measured in v92/hours (France 35 h, Europe 33-40 h)

normative_weeks.note: V6.1 convention, retained only for comparison

insee_full_time_employee_annual_hours_20.note: INSEE, recorded in V6.1 sources.csv; checked by audit/source_verification.csv

scenarios.description: PRIMARY. Usual weekly hours of employees capped at 30; leave/absence pattern (effective weeks) unchanged; self-employed unchanged
ALTERNATIVE RULE: usual weekly hours of employees capped at 35 (France's legal reference week enforced as an actual cap); self-employed unchanged
As primary, cap also applied to self-employed and family workers
SENSITIVITY: as primary, but full-time employees work 2 extra weeks/year because RTT days compensating >35h would lapse (synthetic magnitude)
V6.1 convention: annual hours of full-time employees capped at 30 x 46 weeks; part-time unchanged unless above
V6.1 convention applied to all workers
SENSITIVITY: 15% of part-timers assumed to usually work 32h (synthetic tail; LFS gives only group means)
SENSITIVITY: 35h cap (France's legal reference duration, not a UNIRA rule)

labour_reserve._comment: Mobilisation of people not working today into 30h jobs. Shares are UPPER bounds (full take-up, perfect matching).

entrant_relative_productivity.note: 1.0 = entrants as productive per hour as incumbents (upper bound); 0.75 illustrates lower experience/skills match. Not estimated.

evidence_pathway._comment: Combines sector-specific theta (audit/hours_productivity_evidence.md) with labour-reserve mobilisation (benchmark framing). Take-up is SYNTHETIC: no evaluated reform shows hours cuts alone create net jobs, so mobilisation requires deliberate policy (training, care services, accessible jobs).

35._comment: 39->35 is the range actually evaluated (Aubry laws, Portugal): theta 0.2-0.6, upper end from subsidised volunteer firms (audit/hours_productivity_evidence.md)
